label: Sparse: first copy step re-inputting n/s/f/q/l/w in short sequences (low precision)
explanation: Sparse feature (~0.08% of steps). 77% of mass is in the copy phase, concentrated at recall_idx 1-2 (the step right after <DEL>, where the input is orig(0)) in short sequences (L=3-5). The input token is usually n (strongest), s, f, q, l or w. Top examples look like "n b j <DEL> [n] b": input n, next output b/u/g, last original token often j. The other ~23% fires in the original phase, mostly on one of the same tokens right after j. Activation is higher for short L and for input n, but no simple conjunction picks it out: the best predicate (recall_idx==1, input in {n,s,f,q,l,w}, L<=5) gets dev precision 0.07, recall 0.45, mass recall 0.47. Adding conditions on the output token or L<=4 raises precision only to about 0.26 and loses recall. The feature seems to depend on a combination of specific tokens rather than one describable property. It never fires at t=0,1 or on the delimiter, and almost never once the copy has gone wrong.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=2 & prev_tok=j (+6.69), t=3 & prev_tok=j (+5.56), phase=2 & in_tok=n (+4.55), in_tok=f (+3.82), prev2_tok=j (+3.80), in_tok=q (+3.50). Lower it: next_out=v (-3.54), next_out=k (-3.34), orig0=3 (-2.91), out_tok=t (-2.73).
